results.content: # What Should Basic Terms and Conditions Include? Terms and Conditions govern the contractual relationship between you and your users and set the way in which your product, service or content may be used, in a **legally binding** way. **Terms typically contain copyright clauses, disclaimers and terms of sale, allow you to set governing law, list mandatory consumer protection clauses, and more.**. Because the Terms & Conditions document is essentially a legally binding agreement; it is, therefore, not only important to have one in place, but also necessary to ensure that it meets legal requirements. **This means that the document must be up-to-date with all applicable regulations, precise, visible and easily understandable so that users can both easily see it and agree to it.** The “agreeing action” should be done in an unambiguous way (e.g. clicking a checkbox with a visible link to the document before being able to create an account or use the service). While the full content may vary based on the particulars of your business, the Terms and Conditions should at least include the following:. * **Safety** information, including instructions for **proper use** (where applicable). * **Terms of delivery** of product/service (where applicable). * **Rights of use** (if applicable). * **Conditions of use**/ purchase (eg. * **Refund policy/exchange/termination of service** and related info. ##### Note on terms and conditions templates. One of the questions we’ve come across from time to time is *“Can I just use a terms and conditions template?”*. Despite how simple they appear, terms and conditions are meant to meet incredibly complex and highly specific scenarios. Because each terms and conditions document is a **legally binding contract that is meant to protect you, the business owner**, it’s critically important that the document matches your specific business processes, model, and remains up-to-date with the various laws referenced in its contents. results.title: Literary Contracts Checklist: Essential Clauses and Terms to Include
results.content: # Literary Contracts Checklist: Essential Clauses and Terms to Include. These legal documents define the rights, responsibilities, and obligations of each party involved in the publication and distribution of literary works. As an author, understanding the key clauses and terms to include in your literary contracts is paramount to protect your intellectual property, secure fair compensation, and ensure a successful and mutually beneficial partnership. In this blog post, we will explore the essential clauses that should be part of every literary contract, empowering you with the knowledge needed to navigate the publishing landscape confidently. The grant of rights clause is the cornerstone of a literary contract. It specifies which rights the author is granting to the publisher. Clarifying the scope and duration of these rights ensures that the author retains control over their work and can negotiate fair compensation for each usage. A transparent and fair royalty and compensation clause is essential for authors to receive adequate financial rewards for their literary endeavors. This clause should outline the percentage of royalties the author will receive from book sales, subsidiary rights, and any other revenue streams. The delivery and publication schedule sets clear deadlines for the author to submit their manuscript and for the publisher to release the book. Authors should retain full copyright ownership of their works while granting the necessary rights for publication. Authors should include a termination and rights reversion clause that allows them to terminate the contract under certain circumstances, such as the publisher's failure to meet contractual obligations. This clause should also outline the process for reverting rights back to the author upon termination. A well-crafted literary contract is essential for any author seeking success in the publishing world. By including these essential clauses in their agreements, authors can protect their intellectual property, secure fair compensation, and maintain creative control over their works. At Douglas Law, our legal team understands the intricacies of literary contracts and the importance of safeguarding your rights as an author. Armed with this literary contract checklist and the support of Douglas Law, authors can embark on their publishing journey with confidence and focus on what they do best—creating remarkable literature for the world to enjoy.

results.content: Your Terms & Conditions (T&C) can be called Terms of Use or Terms of Service, but no matter the title of your agreement, this agreement **contains all the rules between you and the users** who are using your website or app. What Clauses Should My Terms and Conditions Agreement Include? A Terms and Conditions agreement is a legal agreement that sets out the terms of the relationship between you - the business owner, and your end users or customers. It will disclose things such as payment terms, what laws govern any legal disputes under the agreement, how the agreement can be terminated, what users cannot do while using your website or service, and so on. ## What Clauses Should My Terms and Conditions Agreement Include? Your Terms & Conditions agreement is not enforceable unless the user accepts the agreement. The Terms & Conditions are the ground rules of use for your website and app, so it's a good practice to integrate and reference your other policies and legal agreements, such as Privacy Policy, Cookies Policy or others. **A "User Submissions" clause in your Terms & Conditions agreement** is only relevant for websites and apps that encourage user-generated content. ### Clause 9: Applicable Law. The **"Applicable Law" clause in your Terms & Conditions agreement** informs what jurisdiction applies when it comes to disputes and the terms of the legal agreement. Your Terms & Conditions agreement is there to protect your business and one way you can enforce it is by terminating access to abusive users through a "Termination" clause. Through a "Changes to Terms" or "Amendments" clause you have a way to inform users when the Terms & Conditions agreement is changed. Terms and Conditions (also known as Terms of Use or Terms of Service agreements) are important legal documents that outline the rights and responsibilities of both you and your users. ### Terms and Conditions for APIs. A Terms and Conditions agreement should include essential clauses that protect your business, define user responsibilities, and mitigate potential legal risks. This article will walk you through the key clauses every business owner needs in their T&C, giving you clear explanations and real-world examples to help you create a strong and effective document. ## What Key Clauses Should Your Terms and Conditions Agreement Include? Some key clauses to include in your terms and conditions agreement are:. ## Why Do I Need Account Terms and User Eligibility Clauses? You need account terms and user eligibility clauses to define who can use your services and under what conditions. Your Acceptable Use clause gets into the specifics of what users cannot do while using your service. This type of clause is necessary because it protects your business reputation and helps prevent legal issues arising from user misconduct. If your business involves transactions, your payment terms clause needs to specify how you accept payments. A limitation of liability and disclaimer of warranties clause is crucial for managing risk and setting realistic expectations with your users. Your T&C should clearly define the conditions under which you or the user can terminate the agreement. First, this clause should explain when you might terminate a user's account. A clear termination clause allows you to remove users who cause problems or violate your rules. Your terms and conditions should specify which jurisdiction's laws will govern the agreement and the process for resolving any possible disputes. You need a clause outlining how you will notify users of your Terms and Conditions changes. This clause explains how you'll inform users about these changes. It's also important to state that a user's continued use of your service after the changes go live signifies their acceptance of the new terms. A clear modification clause allows you to adapt your terms as your business evolves or legal requirements change. A comprehensive Terms and Conditions agreement protects your business and sets clear expectations with your users. * A clause on modifications (how you'll update the terms).
